summary: Diagnostic of the intermittent ProbeGracefulRejectionClientTest failure at exact head 3c73a59743e3dfe4b5ae5e11b0cdbe8c1e8fcae6, seed 17764C0DE, on this 2-core Linux host. REPRODUCTION IS CERTAIN AND THE PRODUCTION LOGIC IS EXONERATED; the exact connection-close trigger inside the JDK client's transport was not isolated to one line of behavior, and none of the three candidate corrections eliminated the failure, so per the job's own verdict rule this files as incomplete rather than passed. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: (1) The failure reproduces in full-class runs at roughly 1 in 5 unloaded and 1 in 3 under two-core CPU load: 10 failing runs captured today across configurations, plus the 2 of 6 in the r4 gate. Isolated single-method runs pass (4/4 for the forged method). (2) The victim WANDERS: testForgedMarkerOnApplication503AuthorizesRetry (r4 runs 3-4, two further captures), testMarkerIsIgnoredWithoutExplicitTrust (twice), testOneShotIteratorIsNotResent (once, a JDK-client-only method), testMarkedRejectionRetriesMaterializedUpdateOnce (three times). One loaded run failed two methods. No victim is specific to the forged marker; the r4 framing against that one method was sampling. (3) Every stack-bearing capture is a JDK HttpClient send: HttpJdkSolrClient.requestWithBaseUrl via LBSolrClient.doRequest, root cause java.io.IOException: Broken pipe at sun.nio.ch.SocketDispatcher.writev0, surfaced as 'HTTP/1.1 header parser received no bytes'. No failing stack involves the Jetty client. (4) Server-side instrumentation proves the lost request NEVER REACHES THE SERVER: passing runs receive 32 requests (11 HEAD probes, 20 POST, 1 GET, all completing, zero failed callbacks); failing runs receive exactly 30, with all 11 HEAD probes present and the failing iteration's submissions missing. In no failing run was an update replayed after an ambiguous send; the class's central safety property held in every capture. (5) A capture with the JDK client's own connection logging enabled shows the failing POST dispatched on the pooled connection the client had just used for its one-time HEAD probe ('Returning connection to the pool', then POST, then Broken pipe on write, then the client closes the connection isOpen=false): the server side had already closed that connection. The HEAD probes themselves carry the JDK client's first-request h2c upgrade offer (Upgrade: h2c, HTTP2-Settings) against fixture connectors that have no HTTP/2 factory, and Jetty's graceful-rejection responses in the same runs intermittently carry 'connection: close'. (6) REFUTED by discriminating campaign: the fixture writing a body for HEAD. With HEAD answered headers-only, 4 of 12 loaded runs still failed with the identical signature. Sequential raw-socket wire probes (with and without the upgrade headers) never reproduce the close; it needs the client's real dispatch timing under load. (7) REFUTED as a correction: making the fixture connectors HTTP/2-capable (requires a new solrj test dependency plus lockfile update). The JDK client then upgrades for real and the class's HTTP/1.1 assertions fail deterministically in 4 methods with no Broken pipe; it changes the protocol under test. (8) NOT A CURE: pinning the fixture's JDK clients to HTTP/1.1 with .useHttp1_1(true) at the three producer-builder sites, mirroring the Jetty side's existing pin: 1 of 12 loaded runs still failed, in the forged method, identical signature. The reduction from the ~1-in-3 loaded base rate is within noise at these sample sizes. REMAINING UNKNOWN: whether the server-side close originates in Jetty 12.1.14's connection handling for a first request that offered an upgrade it cannot honor, in its graceful-rejection connection handling, or in loopback behavior under CPU starvation; this host has no packet-capture tooling, which is the next discriminating step. PROPOSED MINIMAL CORRECTION for the branch owner, in order: (a) document the instability in the class as a JDK-transport/fixture race on loaded hosts and treat a single no-bytes failure in this class as a rerun signal, not a branch defect; no production change, no assertion change, no added retry is justified by any evidence gathered; (b) if it must be chased further, capture packets on a host with tcpdump during a loaded failing run and correlate FIN/RST timing with the client log. Diagnostic only, per the job: no source was pushed and no public comment was made; the disposable clone was restored to the exact head (git status clean) and all instrumentation and candidate patches are preserved in the evidence tarball.
